rule:
Every stair must have risers between 100 mm and 180 mm high.
Regulatory text (the authoritative clauses - use them to interpret the requirement and its applicability; you must still work out how to read or measure it from the IFC):
ADA and ABA Accessibility Guidelines (2004), 504.2 Treads and Risers: All steps on a flight of stairs shall have uniform riser heights and uniform tread depths. Risers shall be 4 inches (100 mm) high minimum and 7 inches (180 mm) high maximum. Treads shall be 11 inches (280 mm) deep minimum.
Benchmark convention: judge every stair as a whole, from its steps as modelled in its geometry; recorded step properties may be missing, zero or inconsistent with the geometry. The limits apply in inches as written: 4 in = 101.6 mm and 7 in = 177.8 mm. A stair fails when its typical riser height (the height shared by its regular steps) is below 101.6 mm or above 177.8 mm. A first or last step that differs from the others is covered by a separate uniformity check, and tread depth by a separate tread check.

Label every stair.
Report the GlobalId of every element (modelled as IfcStair) that does NOT satisfy this requirement.

solibri.configuration: The four rule sets of the EC3-2026 Solibri projects (ADA and ABA Accessibility Guidelines, Advanced Space Check, BIM Validation - Architectural, General Space Check) with their classifications, unchanged. EC3 models: their arc.smc; other models: ec3_template.smc (the EC3 smiley_west project with the model replaced through Update Models). Report template CheckingSummaryTemplate - Issue and Components.

reference.policy: FAIL: a scope element listed by an issue of the Solibri rule whose text matches the message; PASS: every other scope element.
reference.limitations: The geometric judgement is Solibri's and is not recomputed independently.
